extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students (or learners) preparing for/taking MIT OpenCourseWare Algebra I
extracted.subtask_description: Syllabus for an undergraduate Algebra I course (MIT OpenCourseWare) describing meeting times, prerequisites, textbook, topics, expectations for preparation, grading breakdown, homework policy, and collaboration rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear Algebra (18.700), Analysis I (18.100), or permission of instructor. Students should have some familiarity with proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though students need to be comfortable with matrix operations, the course won’t go over the first chapter on matrices systematically. Students should plan to study this chapter on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Textbook
rubrics_metrics.description: Artin, M. Algebra (2nd Edition). Addison Wesley, 2010. ISBN: 9780132413770.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated course text for readings and exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course Description / Topics
rubrics_metrics.description: This undergraduate level Algebra I course covers groups, vector spaces, linear transformations, symmetry groups, bilinear forms, and linear groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class Preparation Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are expected to prepare for each class meeting by completing the assigned readings and exercises for each topic prior to class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparation is required even though some exercises will not be collected; completing them beforehand supports class participation and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercises Not Turned In or Graded
rubrics_metrics.description: However, the exercises will not be turned in or graded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises are for in-class preparation and practice rather than for direct grade credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grading Breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Grading for the course will be based on the following: Homework problems 25%; Three quizzes (25% each) 75%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines how course performance is quantified (homework contributes 25%, quizzes together 75%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quizzes Availability Note
rubrics_metrics.description: *Please note: the quizzes are not available for this version of the course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although quizzes are part of the stated grading scheme, the provided materials for this OCW version do not include the quizzes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework Problems — Importance and Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: The homework problems are the most important part of the course. Many of the problems are extensive and difficult, and require hard work. They are not meant to be completed in one sitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homework is substantial and central to learning outcomes; students should allocate significant time and may need multiple sessions to finish problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homework Collaboration and Attribution Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Students are encouraged to get together with other students to work on these assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When collaborating, students must list their collaborators at the top of their assignment solutions.
